This page is for *after* class, before the homework: one problem type run
twice — **fully worked** (every step narrated, including the why), then a
**faded twin** where the middle steps are yours, each confirmed by a gate
before the next appears. Finish the twin without the Show-me button and
the homework will feel familiar. Ungraded; classmates encouraged.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-reveal-all"></div>
```

## Part 1 — fully worked: the inclined gate

*A rectangular gate, 2 m wide and 4 m along its slope, lies at 60° to the
horizontal with its top edge at the water surface. Hinge along the top
edge, stop along the bottom. Find the resultant, its location, and the
stop reaction.*

**Step 0 — the plan.** Every plane-surface problem is the same three
purchases: force from the centroid, location from the moment, reactions
from statics. *Slant coordinates* (distance $y$ along the plate) keep the
bookkeeping clean; convert to depth only when pressure needs it.

**Step 1 — force.** Centroid: mid-plate, $\bar y = 2$ m slant → depth
$\bar h = 2\sin 60° = 1.73$ m. Then
$F_R = \rho g \bar h A = 998(9.81)(1.73)(8) = 136$ kN.
The average bill, times the area — the incline entered only through
$\bar h$.

**Step 2 — location.** $y_{cp} = \bar y + I_{xc}/(\bar y A)$ with
$I_{xc} = bL^3/12 = 10.7$ m⁴:
$y_{cp} = 2 + 10.7/16 = 2.67$ m down the slope — two-thirds of
a meter below the centroid, because deeper fluid pushes harder.

**Step 3 — the stop.** Moments about the hinge (top edge, slant origin):
$R_{stop} \cdot 4 = F_R \cdot y_{cp}$, so
$R_{stop} = 136(2.67)/4 = 90.5$ kN. The stop
carries 67% of the load — the deep end always pays more.

## Part 2 — the faded twin: the submerged vertical gate

*A vertical gate 1.5 m wide × 2 m tall, top edge **1.0 m below** the
surface. Hinge at top, stop at bottom. Same three purchases — your turn.*

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 1a — centroid depth of the gate?"
     data-answer="2.0" data-tol="0.02" data-units="m"
     data-hint="Top edge at 1.0 m, gate 2 m tall: centroid halfway down the gate."
     data-solution="h̄ = 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0 m."
     data-target="u3w-s2"></div>
```

::: {#u3w-s2 .fl-hidden}
```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 1b — resultant force?"
     data-answer="58.8" data-tol="0.03" data-units="kN"
     data-hint="ρg h̄ A with A = 3 m². The submergence entered through h̄ — nothing else changes."
     data-solution="F = 998 × 9.81 × 2.0 × 3 = 58.8 kN."
     data-target="u3w-s3"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u3w-s3 .fl-hidden}
✓ Now the location. Vertical gate: slant coordinate = depth, so $\bar y = 2.0$ m.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 2 — depth of the center of pressure?"
     data-answer="2.17" data-tol="0.02" data-units="m"
     data-hint="y_cp = ȳ + I/(ȳA) with I = bL³/12 = 1.0 m⁴. Deep submergence shrinks the correction — watch how small it is now."
     data-solution="y_cp = 2.0 + 1.0/(2×3) = 2.17 m — only 17 cm below the centroid, vs 67 cm for Part 1's surface-piercing gate."
     data-target="u3w-s4"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u3w-s4 .fl-hidden}
✓ The correction $I/(\bar yA)$ dies as $\bar y$ grows: deeply drowned
gates feel nearly uniform pressure.

```{=html}
<div class="fl-checkpoint"
     data-prompt="Step 3 — reaction at the bottom stop (hinge at the top edge, 1.0 m depth)?"
     data-answer="34.3" data-tol="0.03" data-units="kN"
     data-hint="Moment about the hinge: R × 2 = F × (y_cp − 1.0). The moment arm is measured from the hinge, not the surface."
     data-solution="R = 58.8 × (2.17 − 1.0)/2 = 34.3 kN — just over half the load, because the CP sits barely past mid-gate."
     data-target="u3w-s5"></div>
```
:::

::: {#u3w-s5 .fl-hidden}
**What transferred.** Centroid → force; moment → location; statics →
reactions. The only thing submergence changed was *how far below the
centroid* the resultant rides — the deeper the gate, the more democratic
the pressure.
:::

## Let the toolbox referee

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: false
from fluidtools.hydrostat import PlaneSurface, gate_hinge_reaction
gA = PlaneSurface('rectangle', b=2.0, L=4.0, y_top=0.0, theta_deg=60)
gB = PlaneSurface('rectangle', b=1.5, L=2.0, y_top=1.0, theta_deg=90)
for name, gg in [("Part 1 (inclined, surface-piercing)", gA),
                 ("Part 2 (vertical, submerged)", gB)]:
    R, F = gate_hinge_reaction(gg, 'top')
    print(f"{name}: F = {F/1000:.1f} kN, stop reaction = {R/1000:.1f} kN")
```
